response: The prognosis of low-tone sudden deafness does not inevitably progress to Meniere's disease. Research suggests that not all patients with low-tone sudden deafness will develop endolymphatic hydrops, even if they experience vertigo attacks at the onset. Electrocochleography (ECochG) can be a useful tool in determining the prognosis of these patients. This means that while there may be some similarities between low-tone sudden deafness and Meniere's disease, they are not the same condition, and the progression from one to the other is not guaranteed.
